newsitem.title: SPAIN: World bank looks at ways to help Albania.
newsitem.headline: World bank looks at ways to help Albania.

text.p: The president of the World Bank said on Thursday that the World Bank, together with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), was looking at ways to help stabilise the situation in crisis-stricken Albania.

"We are of course involved in the Balkan region and are particularly concerned with the situation in Albania. Together with the IMF we are looking at ways in which we can assist the government in terms of stabilising the situation in the country," James Wolfensohn told reporters in Madrid.
Wolfensohn added that help would be ready as soon as the political situation became clearer.
"..as soon as the government gets in it's possible for us to be able to offer quickly the assistance of the financial system," said Wolfenshon.

On Monday, the parliament re-elected president Sali Berisha for a second term. The assembly, where Berisha's Democratic Party holds nearly all the seats, introduced a state of emergency early this week.
The World Bank president was in Madrid to sign an agreement of closer cooperation with the Spanish government.
